text_blocks.snippet: Excessive alcohol consumption can negatively impact kidney health and increase the risk of kidney disease. While the kidneys can sometimes recover from alcohol damage, especially with early intervention and abstinence, severe, long-term damage may not be fully reversible.
snippet_highlighted_words: Excessive alcohol consumption can negatively impact kidney health and increase the risk of kidney disease

list.title: Acute Kidney Injury (AKI):
list.snippet: Binge drinking or heavy alcohol consumption can cause a sudden decline in kidney function, known as AKI. This happens when the kidneys struggle to process the alcohol and its byproducts, leading to an imbalance of fluids and electrolytes.

list.title: Chronic Kidney Disease (CKD):
list.snippet: Long-term, excessive alcohol use can contribute to CKD, a condition where the kidneys lose their ability to filter blood effectively. Alcohol can exacerbate existing risk factors for CKD, such as high blood pressure and diabetes.

list.title: Alcoholic Nephropathy:
list.snippet: This is a specific condition caused by chronic alcohol abuse, resulting in damage to the kidney's structure and function, potentially leading to kidney failure.
